mission.title: security-compliance: [Feat]: Option to skip upstream sync for tags already present locally with onDemand: true
mission.description: [Feat]: Option to skip upstream sync for tags already present locally with onDemand: true. Community-requested feature.

steps.title: Check current security-compliance deployment
steps.description:
Verify your security-compliance version and configuration:
```bash
kubectl get pods -n security-compliance -l app.kubernetes.io/name=security-compliance
helm list -n security-compliance 2>/dev/null || echo "Not installed via Helm"
```
This feature requires a working security-compliance installation.

steps.title: Review security-compliance configuration
steps.description:
Inspect the relevant security-compliance configuration:
```bash
kubectl get all -n security-compliance -l app.kubernetes.io/name=security-compliance
kubectl get configmap -n security-compliance -l app.kubernetes.io/part-of=security-compliance
```
### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

I use zot as a pull-through cache on embedded servers with intermittent connectivity, low bandwidth, and limited disk space.

steps.title: Apply the fix for [Feat]: Option to skip upstream sync for tags already…
Upgrade security-compliance to include the fix
steps.description:
If the fix is included in a newer release, upgrade security-compliance:
```bash
helm repo update
helm upgrade security-compliance security-compliance/security-compliance --namespace security-compliance
```
Verify the upgrade:
```bash
kubectl get pods -n security-compliance
helm list -n security-compliance
```

steps.title: Verify the feature works
steps.description:
Test that the new capability is working as expected:
```bash
kubectl get pods -n security-compliance -l app.kubernetes.io/name=security-compliance
kubectl get events -n security-compliance --sort-by='.lastTimestamp' | tail -10
```
Confirm the feature described in "[Feat]: Option to skip upstream sync for tags already…" is functioning correctly.

resolution.summary: With `onDemand`, zot checks a stored tag against upstream on each request. For tags that don't change once pushed, such as release versions, this check only adds latency, and the request fails or waits when the upstream is slow or unreachable.
codeSnippets:
upstream                     tag                     result
answers 503                  1.38 (synced)           200 in 1 ms, 0 upstream requests
answers 503                  1.36 (copied in)        200 in 1 ms, 0 upstream requests
accepts, never answers       1.38, 1.36              200 in 1 ms
same, downstream restarted   1.38, 1.36              200 in 1 ms
back up                      1.37 (not stored)       200 (synced)

prerequisites.description: A running Kubernetes cluster with security-compliance installed or the issue environment reproducible.
